note: Prevention for a lint engine whose rules knob (the names its routed rule traits answer LINT_FOUND with) differs from what they emit. The routed trait declarations come from the call sites input (references, else an inline trait); each declaration's transition and tick effects are walked for emit LINT_FOUND { rule: <literal> }. Which rules answer the program pass only (programOnlyRules) cannot be derived structurally, so it is only checked to be a subset of rules.

findings.message: the rule b is answered by a routed trait but missing from rules: a pass never expects it, so it can settle before b answered
the rules entry c is answered by no routed trait: a pass waits for it and never settles
the rules entry a is listed more than once
the programOnlyRules entry z is not in rules, so no pass expects it
findings.suggestion: remove z from programOnlyRules or add it to rules

findings.message: the trait R9 routes its LINT_FOUND into Engine but no declaration of it is among the references or the inline traits, so the rule names it answers with are unknown
findings.suggestion: compose R9 through a trait reference the call sites input resolves

findings.message: the trait R1 emits LINT_FOUND with a rule that is not a literal string, so the names the engine must list cannot be read
findings.suggestion: emit LINT_FOUND with a literal string rule
